 `./pitfalls/tmux-resurrect-agents.md`

```text
1	# tmux-resurrect doesn't restore coding-agent / TUI sessions
2	
3	**Symptoms** (grep this section): after `tmux kill-server` + reattach, the
4	window layout and cwd come back but `opencode` / `claude` / `codex` /
5	`aider` / `lazygit` / `btop` / `yazi` panes are just a bare shell prompt;
6	nvim panes restore fine; `tmux-continuum` ran on schedule; `prefix +
7	Ctrl-r` doesn't help.
8	**First seen**: 2026-04, tmux-resurrect master + tmux-continuum master
9	**Affects**: every TUI not in resurrect's default whitelist (effectively:
10	every coding agent, every "modern" TUI shipped after ~2018)
11	**Status**: workaround in place (`@resurrect-processes` extended in
12	`common.conf`); not a bug — by design.
13	
14	## Symptom
15	
16	After kicking the tmux server (manual `tmux kill-server`, OS reboot,
17	ghostty crash, plugin reload that needed full restart):
18	
19	```bash
20	tmux attach
21	# (window layouts come back; nvim re-opens with the same files)
22	# but agent panes show:
23	~/proj/foo $ █
24	# instead of:
25	opencode> █
26	```
27	
28	`tmux-continuum` saved successfully (check `~/.local/share/tmux/resurrect/`
29	or `~/.tmux/resurrect/` — last save file is recent and contains the agent
30	process names). It just chose not to restart them.
31	
32	## Root cause
33	
34	`tmux-resurrect`'s restore phase walks each saved pane, reads the recorded
35	process command, and **only re-execs commands that match the
36	`@resurrect-processes` whitelist**. Default whitelist is approximately:
37	
38	```
39	"~vi vim nvim emacs man less more tail top htop irssi mutt"
40	```
41	
42	Notice what's missing: every coding agent, every git/docker TUI, every
43	modern file manager. `nvim` survives because it's explicitly listed; `vim`
44	survives because of the leading `~` semantics; `htop` survives.
45	`opencode` doesn't survive because it's not on the list — resurrect leaves
46	that pane as a fresh shell at the saved cwd.
47	
48	This is **deliberate**. From the resurrect docs and design discussion
49	([tmux-plugins/tmux-resurrect#9][1]):
50	
51	- Agents typically have **in-memory state** (conversation buffer, MCP
52	  connections, OAuth tokens) that bare `exec opencode` cannot recreate.
53	- Re-execing arbitrary commands is a foot-gun: a daemon launched with `&`,
54	  a `npm run dev` that mutates files, a `psql` connected to prod — none
55	  of these should auto-restart on tmux reattach.
56	- The whitelist is opt-in so the user takes explicit responsibility for
57	  "yes, this command is safe to bare-restart".
58	
59	[1]: https://github.com/tmux-plugins/tmux-resurrect/blob/master/docs/restoring_programs.md
60	
61	## Workaround
62	
63	Extend the whitelist in `dot_config/tmux/common.conf`:
64	
65	```tmux
66	set -g @resurrect-processes 'opencode claude codex aider gemini lazygit btop htop yazi k9s lazydocker glow'
67	```
68	
69	What this **does** restore:
70	
71	- pane re-execs the bare command (no args)
72	- agent picks up at the cwd that was saved
73	- visible result: panel shows the agent's startup screen instead of `$`
74	
75	What this does **not** restore:
76	
77	- conversation history (every coding agent restarts as a brand-new session;
78	  `opencode --continue` / `claude --continue` would resume the last one but
79	  resurrect can't pass args)
80	- in-flight tool calls / pending diffs / sub-agent state
81	- auth tokens that were typed at runtime (those that come from env / config
82	  files survive; runtime `/login` does not)
83	- TUI scroll position / search history
84	
85	If you want session continuity (not just "agent is running again"), wrap
86	each agent in a `*-resume` shim that invokes `--continue`:
87	
88	```bash
89	#!/usr/bin/env bash
90	# ~/.local/bin/opencode-resume
91	exec opencode --continue "$@"
92	```
93	
94	then `set -g @resurrect-processes 'opencode-resume claude-resume codex-resume ...'`.
95	Trade-off: the very first launch in any session also goes through
96	`--continue` which may resume an unrelated old session if you forgot to
97	explicitly `opencode` (no `-resume`) for new work. Repo currently uses the
98	plain whitelist (option a) and leaves the wrapper variant (option c) to
99	the user.
100	
101	## Prevention
102	
103	When adopting a new TUI / coding-agent CLI, decide upfront:
104	
105	1. **Safe to bare re-exec** (file managers, git TUIs, monitors, agents you
106	   always want to restart from scratch) → add to `@resurrect-processes`.
107	2. **Stateful and worth resuming** (agents with conversation continuity
108	   that matters) → write a `<tool>-resume` wrapper, whitelist that.
109	3. **Dangerous to auto-restart** (dev servers, prod connections, anything
110	   with side effects on launch) → leave off the whitelist; restore brings
111	   you to a shell at the right cwd, you launch by hand.
112	
113	The line between (1) and (2) is judgement; "I want my agent panes to look
114	populated after reattach" is a valid reason to pick (1) even for stateful
115	agents — you accept that the visible session is fresh.
116	
117	## Verifying after a change
118	
119	```bash
120	# After editing common.conf:
121	chezmoi apply ~/.config/tmux
122	tmux source-file ~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf
123	tmux show-options -g | grep resurrect-processes
124	# expect to see your extended list
125	
126	# Force a save + restore cycle without losing real sessions:
127	tmux run-shell ~/.tmux/plugins/tmux-resurrect/scripts/save.sh
128	# (do NOT run restore.sh from a live session — it spawns NEW panes for
129	# every saved pane on top of your current state)
130	
131	# Inspect the latest save file to confirm the agent commands were captured:
132	ls -t ~/.local/share/tmux/resurrect/last 2>/dev/null \
133	  || ls -t ~/.tmux/resurrect/last
134	cat $(readlink ~/.local/share/tmux/resurrect/last 2>/dev/null \
135	  || readlink ~/.tmux/resurrect/last) | grep -E 'opencode|claude'
136	```
137	
138	The real verification is to `tmux kill-server` and reattach — but obviously
139	only do that when you've finished work you care about.
140
```
</details></tool-use>

95	# Window activity / silence / bell flags
96	# These drive the per-window flag glyphs (`#` activity, `~` silence, `!` bell)
97	# that Catppuccin's `window-status-format` already includes via #{window_flags}.
98	# Use case: glance at the tab bar to see which non-current window produced
99	# output (`#`) or has been quiet for a while (`~`). Useful for long builds /
100	# tests / pueue queues running in background panes.
101	#
102	# Limitation for LLM agent panes: opencode/claude run a spinner while the
103	# model is thinking, so from tmux's POV the pane is *always* active —
104	# `monitor-silence` will not fire for "agent waiting on user". For true
105	# semantic state (running / idle / error) on agent panes, see
106	# backlog/tmux-window-status-indicators.md.
107	#
108	# `visual-*` are kept off so the message line never spams; the flag in the
109	# tab list is the only visible signal.
110	setw -g monitor-activity on
111	setw -g monitor-bell on
112	setw -g monitor-silence 0
113	set -g visual-activity off
114	set -g visual-silence off
115	set -g visual-bell off
116

118	# multi-word confirmations like "Moved to foo:3 (zsh)" before they vanish.
119	# 0 = stay until the next key event (the key still does its normal action;
120	# only the message gets cleared). Trade-off: occasionally a stale message
121	# lingers if you stop typing, but no important confirmation is ever missed.

132	set -s extended-keys always

134	  'set -s extended-keys-format csi-u'
135	set -as terminal-features 'xterm*:extkeys'

139	
140	# Declare OSC 52 support explicitly for common outer terminals. tmux 3.2+ only
141	# emits OSC 52 when it believes the outer terminal supports it; most modern
142	# terminals (Ghostty, Alacritty, iTerm2, kitty, WezTerm) do. Without these

145	# apps (e.g. Neovim over SSH) silently drop.
146	set -as terminal-features ",xterm*:clipboard"

剛好這台 Mac 今天 16:54 真的有一份 tmux 的 crash report，正好可以當示範。

## 1. tmux crash 的 debug 方法（按好用程度排）

**A. macOS 自帶的 crash report**（這次直接命中）
路徑 `~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/tmux-*.ips` — 是 JSON-on-line-1 + JSON 主體的格式。剛才那份顯示：

- 訊號：`SIGABRT` (`Abort trap: 6`)
- 原因：`___BUG_IN_CLIENT_OF_LIBMALLOC_POINTER_BEING_FREED_WAS_NOT_ALLOCATED`（double-free / invalid free，libmalloc 自爆）
- 觸發路徑：`cmd_copy_mode_exec` → `window_pane_set_mode` → `window_copy_init` → `window_copy_clone_screen` → `screen_reinit` → `grid_clear_lines` → `grid_free_line` → abort
- 父行程：alacritty

也就是說，這是**進入 copy-mode 時 tmux 自身在釋放 grid line 出現了 heap 損毀**，屬於 tmux 上游 bug。和 plugin、`@resurrect-processes`、agent 都沒關係。最務實的處理是 `brew upgrade tmux`、看 [tmux/tmux issues](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/issues) 有沒有 `grid_free_line` / `window_copy_clone_screen` 相關 fix；如果還能重現，就把 `.ips` 貼到 issue 裡。

**B. `log show` 撈系統訊息**（適合「沒有 .ips、但確實 server 死了」）
```bash
log show --predicate 'process == "tmux"' --info --last 2h
log show --predicate 'sender == "Symptoms" AND eventMessage CONTAINS "tmux"' --last 2h
```
能看到 OOM、被 jetsam 殺、signal 來源。

**C. tmux 自己的 verbose log**
```bash
tmux kill-server
tmux -vv new -s debug
# 同一目錄下會生 tmux-server-*.log / tmux-client-*.log
```
重點是「server 起來後，操作到 crash 為止做了哪些 cmdq」，對應 `.ips` 裡的 `cmd_*_exec` 一條條都會落到 log。

**D. core dump**（最後手段，能 backtrace 全變數）
```bash
ulimit -c unlimited
sudo sysctl kern.coredump=1
# 然後啟 tmux，crash 後 core 在 /cores/
lldb /opt/homebrew/bin/tmux -c /cores/core.<pid>
```

順帶一提，repo 的 `pitfalls/` 目前已有三條和 tmux 崩潰/異常相關的（`tmux-display-menu-silent-fail`、`yazi-tmux-popup-crash`、`tmux-pane-vanishes-on-ctrl-c-despite-shell-wrapper`），但沒有「copy-mode + grid_free_line」這條——如果之後又重現，值得收一條 pitfall。

## 2. VS Code Remote SSH 的「還原」其實是錯覺

這是常見的迷思——VS Code 並沒有真的 restore runtime。它做的是：

1. **VSCode Server 是長駐 daemon**，跟 SSH 連線解耦。client 斷線時 server 還在跑，opencode、build、terminal PTY 全都在那條 server process tree 裡活著。
2. **重連時是 reattach 而不是 restore**——和 `tmux a` 完全一樣的概念。
3. 真要等到 VSCode server 自己死掉（OOM、kill、機器重開），裡面跑的 opencode 一樣會死。它能「revive」的部分只有：把當初啟動 terminal 用的 command line 再跑一次（這就是 tmux-resurrect 在做的事）+ scrollback 序列化還原。

**所以 tmux server 沒掛時** → 你已經和 VSCode 一樣強了，`tmux a` 就回來了。
**tmux server 掛掉時** → VSCode 也一樣只能 re-exec command + 顯示舊 scrollback，**沒人能還原 in-memory state**（OAuth token、conversation buffer、MCP 連線、未存的 nvim buffer）。

這是 OS 層級限制，不是 tmux 的鍋。Linux 上理論可用 CRIU 做 process tree checkpoint，但 macOS 沒有等價物。

## 3. Restore 真的還能再優化的點

按收益 / 工程量排，從高到低：

**(a) 給 agent 加 `*-resume` wrapper（改動最小、收益最大）**
`pitfalls/tmux-resurrect-agents.md` 裡已有設計但沒實作。在 `~/.local/bin/` 放：
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
exec opencode --continue "$@"
```
然後 `@resurrect-processes 'opencode-resume claude-resume codex-resume ...'`。tradeoff：每次新開 pane 也會先嘗試 resume 上一個 session，要靠習慣（手動跑 `opencode` 才是新會話）。**或者** 把這個跟 sesh-/session-name 綁定，每個 session 一個 conversation，會更乾淨。

**(b) `@resurrect-capture-pane-contents 'on'` + `@resurrect-save-shell-history 'on'`**
保存 pane scrollback 和 shell history，重啟後 `prefix + Ctrl-r` restore 時會把當時的 scrollback 重新貼回去。這就是 VSCode 的 "terminal revival" 在做的事。代價：每次 save snapshot 大很多，I/O 比較重。

**(c) 把 `@continuum-save-interval` 從預設 15 分鐘調短到 5 分鐘**
crash 時最多只丟 5 分鐘的 layout 變動。

**(d) 把 conversation 落盤的責任從 tmux 推給 agent 自己**
opencode、claude、codex 三家都有 session DB。`*-resume` wrapper 加上 `--session=$tmux_session_name` 參數（如果 CLI 支援），一個 tmux session 對應一個 agent session，這樣即使是真的重開機都能對得上。需要每個 agent CLI 的具體支持情況逐個驗證。

**(e) 把 cwd / open files 從 nvim 那層也吃乾淨**
nvim 已經被 resurrect 直接 re-exec 了，但「打開了什麼 buffer」沒還原。`vim-obsession` / `mksession` 寫到 `Session.vim`，配合 nvim 啟動參數可以連 buffer / split / cursor 都還原。這個 repo 的 nvim 設定值得加一條。

---

要不要我先實作 (a) 的 `*-resume` wrapper（給 opencode/claude/codex 三家），順便把 (c) 的 `@continuum-save-interval` 調成 5 分鐘？這是改動最小、不會誤傷現有行為的組合。

maintenance contract and [`README.md`](README.md) for current architecture.

> Do not create new `ROADMAP.md` / `IDEAS.md` / `BACKLOG.md` files — `TODO.md` is
> the single backlog index. Long-form research goes in [`backlog/<slug>.md`](backlog/).

## How to read this

Each item carries two tags:

- **Priority**: `P1` (next likely batch) · `P2` (worth doing) · `P3` (someday) · `P?` (needs evaluation first — spike before committing)
- **Effort**: `S` (< 1h) · `M` (half day) · `L` (multi-day) · `XL` (architectural, design doc first)

A trailing `→ [research](backlog/<slug>.md)` link means the item has accompanying
investigation, design notes, or paused troubleshooting — read that first before
re-investigating. Items without a link are simple enough to act on directly.

When implementing an item, move it to the `## Done` section in the same commit
with a one-line summary of what shipped.

Based on the search results, I found relevant information about your query:

tmux 3.6a crashes with a memory allocation error when entering copy mode in long-running sessions on macOS. This is documented in GitHub issue #4777.

The leak is exposed when copy mode attempts to clone the screen buffer, and the error occurs in grid_free_line, attempting to free memory that was already freed (double-free bug). 

The crash details show: "pointer being freed was not allocated" error, with the crash occurring in the call chain: cmd_copy_mode_exec → window_pane_set_mode → window_copy_init → window_copy_clone_screen → screen_reinit → grid_clear_lines → grid_free_line, triggering a SIGABRT signal.

The crash is 100% reproducible and terminal-agnostic, affecting both Alacritty and Ghostty terminals on Apple Silicon Macs.

Based on the search results, I found a highly relevant issue matching your query:

The crash occurs in tmux 3.6a on macOS (Apple Silicon) when entering copy mode, with the call stack showing: cmd_copy_mode_exec → window_pane_set_mode → window_copy_init → window_copy_clone_screen → screen_reinit → grid_clear_lines → grid_free_line [CRASH: double-free]

The double-free bug occurs in grid_free_line when copy mode attempts to clone the screen buffer, attempting to free memory that was already freed. The tmux server crashes with a memory allocation error when entering copy mode in long-running sessions, and the crash is 100% reproducible and terminal-agnostic.

This issue was reported in December 2025 on the tmux GitHub repository (Issue #4777) and affects tmux 3.6a specifically on macOS with Apple Silicon hardware, though it impacts both Alacritty and Ghostty terminals.

## 結論：這就是上游已修但未發佈的已知 bug

我們本地這次的 crash 和 [tmux/tmux#4777](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/issues/4777) 是**完全同一份**：

| 對照點 | 本機 (今天 16:54) | 上游 issue #4777 |
|---|---|---|
| Stack | `cmd_copy_mode_exec → window_pane_set_mode → window_copy_init → window_copy_clone_screen → screen_reinit → grid_clear_lines → grid_free_line` | 一模一樣 |
| 訊號 | SIGABRT, `___BUG_IN_CLIENT_OF_LIBMALLOC_POINTER_BEING_FREED_WAS_NOT_ALLOCATED` | 一模一樣 |
| 二進位 UUID | `1b2d8e7b-bb77-3465-8bab-73f5bbaffe49` | 一模一樣（即 homebrew 3.6a bottle） |
| 終端 | alacritty | 上游報告人涵蓋 alacritty / ghostty / iTerm2，**terminal-agnostic** |
| 平台 | macOS 26.2 / Apple Silicon (Mac16,10) | 同樣 macOS 26.x / Apple Silicon |
| 觸發條件 | session 長跑（`procLaunch` 15:16 → crash 16:54，約 1h40m，但他人最快也有 ~12h） | 上游：8 天 / 25 小時 / 12 小時 / 100 分鐘都有 |

issue 狀態：**CLOSED 2026-01-06**，由維護者 nicm 在 `035a2f35d40628dcfe235179220fc0ede848a195` 修掉，後續有人 build master 跑了兩週都沒復發確認 fix 有效。

### 現狀：fix 還沒進 homebrew stable

`tmux 3.6a` 仍然是 homebrew bottle 的 stable（也就是我們現在 `/opt/homebrew/Cellar/tmux/3.6a` 那一份），fix 在 master 上但沒打 tag。

### 可以 fix 的選項

**A. `brew install tmux --HEAD`（推薦，能用最快路徑止血）**
```bash
tmux kill-server          # 必要：跑著的 server 會 keep 舊 binary in memory
brew install --HEAD tmux  # 自動切到 master，含 fix
```
- 代價：(1) HEAD 不走 bottle，每次 `brew upgrade` 不會自動拉新提交，要 `brew reinstall --HEAD tmux` 才會重新 build。(2) 需要 Xcode CLT（你應該已經有了）。(3) 升級 libevent/ncurses 時 HEAD build 可能 ABI break，得再 reinstall 一次。
- 對 repo 的影響：tmux 目前**不在** `Brewfile.darwin.tmpl`（剛確認過，是你手動 `brew install` 的，`installed_on_request=True`），所以這個改動是純本機，不影響其他 host。等 3.7 釋出後 `brew install tmux` 就回到 stable bottle。

**B. 等 3.7 / 3.6b 釋出（零工作）**
3.6a 是 2025-06，master 自那之後累積很多修正，3.7 預計近期會出。風險：在那之前每次跑 copy-mode 都是俄羅斯輪盤。

**C. 不做事（workaround：避免 copy-mode）**
不實際，daily 用 tmux 一定會進。

我會建議 **A**——這次只跑 1h40m 就中了，比上游平均觸發時間還早，意味著我們比較容易踩到。

### 應該記在 repo 裡的東西

按 CLAUDE.md 的「pitfall 升級 invariant 條件」（recurring across machines / silently corrupts state / non-obvious workaround）這條三項全中。建議：

1. **新增 `pitfalls/tmux-copy-mode-double-free-3.6a.md`**（症狀標題、一字不改的 error string、可 grep）。內容包括上游 issue 連結、修復 commit、為何 homebrew 3.6a bottle 仍中、`brew install --HEAD` 過渡方案、3.7 釋出後切回的指引。
2. **TODO P? entry**：「3.7 釋出後從 `--HEAD` 切回 stable」一行，提醒未來 `brew upgrade tmux` 注意。
3. **不需要動** `dot_config/tmux/common.conf`、`@resurrect-processes`、`devtools` ansible role——那些都不相關（Linux 走 Linuxbrew / appimage 路徑，不會吃到這個 bottle）。
4. **不需要動** CLAUDE.md 的「Tmux ≥ 3.3」 invariant——這條是針對 popup menu 的另一個問題，跟 copy-mode crash 沒關。但可以在新 pitfall 裡 cross-link 提一下「tmux 版本相關問題集中區」。

要不要我：
- (1) 直接幫你 `tmux kill-server && brew install --HEAD tmux`（本機操作，會踢掉所有 tmux session——你要先保存好工作）
- (2) 寫 `pitfalls/tmux-copy-mode-double-free-3.6a.md` + 加 TODO P? 一行
- (3) 兩個都做

我傾向先做 (2)（純文件、零風險、之後升級也用得到），(1) 等你確認手邊沒事可以 kill server 時再動。

Sources:
- [tmux/tmux#4777 — copy-mode crash on macOS 3.6a](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/issues/4777)
- [tmux/tmux#4575 — related window-copy.c memory leak](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/issues/4575) (closed 2025-08, 不同 bug)

1	# Pitfalls
2	
3	Past traps we've stepped on. Symptoms-first knowledge base — the goal is that
4	when a problem recurs (on a new machine, after an upgrade, with a new tool
5	combo), grepping the symptom here lands you on the root cause and workaround
6	in seconds, instead of re-debugging from scratch.
7	
8	This folder is `chezmoi`-ignored (see `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` → `pitfalls/**`); it
9	is repo metadata for maintainers, not user-facing config to deploy.
10	
11	## Pitfalls vs the rest
12	
13	This repo has four sibling surfaces with overlapping shapes; pick the right one:
14	
15	| Surface | Time direction | Question it answers | Access pattern |
16	|---|---|---|---|
17	| `docs/tools/<tool>.md` | Present | "How does this tool work / how do I configure it?" | Read top to bottom |
18	| `docs/this_repo/<topic>.md` | Present | "Why did we architect it this way?" | Read top to bottom |
19	| `pitfalls/<slug>.md` | **Past** | **"I see error X — has this happened before?"** | **Grep symptoms** |
20	| `backlog/<slug>.md` | Future | "We thought about doing Y — what was the analysis?" | Index in `TODO.md` |
21	| `AGENTS.md` Hard invariants | Present | "What rules MUST agents follow?" | Read top to bottom |
22	
23	A pitfall **graduates** to a Hard invariant in `AGENTS.md` when the trap is
24	serious enough that you can't rely on memory or grep — typically when (a) it
25	recurs across machines, (b) it silently corrupts state, or (c) the workaround
26	is non-obvious and easy to undo by accident. When graduating, leave a
27	`pitfalls/<slug>.md` as historical record and link to it from the invariant.
28	
29	## When to add a pitfall doc
30	
31	Add a `pitfalls/<slug>.md` when you've spent more than ~15 minutes on something
32	where the answer wasn't googleable, AND any of:
33	
34	- The symptom is non-obvious from the root cause (`SSH_CONNECTION` cleared
35	  silently → hostname module disappears, no error)
36	- The fix is "do nothing different but in a specific order" (sentinel writes
37	  must come after `wait $pid` for fleet-apply, etc.)
38	- The same trap could be hit by a new agent / new machine / new contributor
39	- An upstream bug exists with no ETA — workaround needs to outlive memory
40	- A specific tool version is required (or forbidden) and the failure mode at
41	  the wrong version is silent / confusing (e.g. tmux 3.2a popup off-screen)
42	
43	## When NOT to add a pitfall doc
44	
45	- Trivially googleable error (the next person will solve in 30 seconds anyway)
46	- Already covered in `docs/tools/<tool>.md` as part of the tool's normal
47	  configuration — cross-link from this README's "Cross-referenced pitfalls"
48	  table below instead of duplicating
49	- Already a `AGENTS.md` Hard invariant — those have higher priority enforcement
50	  (cross-link only)
51	- One-off transient (network glitch, machine-specific config rot) — fix and
52	  move on
53

55	
56	See [`assets/pitfall-doc.md.template`](#) in the
57	[`project-knowledge-harness` skill](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/tree/main/skills/local/project-knowledge-harness),
58	or copy the structure of an existing entry below.
59	
60	Key sections (different from `backlog/` template — symptom-first, not

62	
63	```markdown
64	# <Title describing the SYMPTOM, not the root cause>
65	
66	**Symptoms** (grep this section): <verbatim error messages, observable behaviour>
67	**First seen**: YYYY-MM
68	**Affects**: <tool/version/OS combo>
69	**Status**: workaround documented / fixed upstream in vX.Y / WONTFIX
70	
71	## Symptom
72	
73	Full error messages (verbatim, not paraphrased — preserves grep-ability).
74	Reproduction steps if applicable.
75	
76	## Root cause
77	
78	Why this happens. Reference source, docs, or upstream issue.
79

81	
82	Immediate workaround (commands, config diff). Should be copy-pasteable.
83

```text
1	# tmux display-menu silently doesn't open (no error, no menu)
2	
3	**Symptoms** (grep this section):
4	- `prefix + <key>` bound to `display-menu` does nothing — no popup, no error message, no entry in `tmux show-messages`
5	- `tmux list-keys -T prefix <key>` shows the binding correctly
6	- Other bindings on the same key (e.g. `bind-key … display-message`) fire fine
7	- Right-click pane menus and other simpler `display-menu` invocations still work
8	- Menu opens on a tall terminal, fails on a short one — or works after deleting half the rows
9	- Bisecting a long flat menu by halving the rows reveals the failure depends on **menu length**, not on the bound key (the key was a red herring)
10	
11	**First seen**: 2026-04
12	**Affects**: tmux 3.6a (likely all 3.x), any platform
13	**Status**: workaround documented (script-driven menu with height-aware tier trimming)
14	
15	## Symptom
16	
17	Bound a 50-row `display-menu` to `prefix + Space`, then to `prefix + Enter`, then to `prefix + e`. Each new key would also "not work" — no popup, no error, no log entry. Hours of debugging key encoding (`extended-keys`, `csi-u`, Ghostty `macos-option-as-alt`, upstream tmux/tmux issues #4571 #4147 #4959 #4984) all turned up nothing because **the keys were bound correctly all along**. The actual failure was that the menu was taller than the terminal.
18	
19	Reproduction:
20	
21	```tmux
22	# Bind a long menu (50+ rows) and shrink the terminal vertically.
23	# Above some height threshold: menu opens.
24	# Below it: prefix + key does nothing. No error.
25	bind-key Space display-menu -T 'big' -x R -y P \
26	  "Row 1" 1 "display-message 1" \
27	  "Row 2" 2 "display-message 2" \
28	  ... 50 more rows ...
29	```
30	
31	This is documented behaviour buried in `man tmux`:
32	
33	> If the menu is too large to fit on the terminal, it is not displayed.
34	
35	It also applies in a less obvious way at moderate heights when `-y P` (anchor to status bar) leaves no room above.
36	
37	## Confounding "real but smaller" bugs
38	
39	Bisecting the failing menu surfaced two genuine quoting bugs that **also** broke the menu but were not the root cause of the dominant symptom:
40	
41	1. **`'\;'` as an accelerator key** — tmux stored this as bare `\;` in the binding, then at menu-execution time interpreted it as a command separator, ending `display-menu` early. Subsequent menu rows became arguments to `last-pane`, producing `command last-pane: too many arguments (need at most 0)` — visible in `tmux show-messages` only when the binding was rebuilt, not on every keypress. **Fix**: use a different accelerator key (`P` instead of `'\;'` for "Last pane").
42	2. **`fzf-tmux ... --bind 'ctrl-d:execute(tmux kill-session -t {2..})'` inline in a menu row** — fzf's `{2..}` range syntax collides with tmux's command-block delimiters `{ }`, silently aborting parse of that row. **Fix**: extract complex commands into shell scripts (no nested-quote disasters in a real shell).
43	
44	Both fixes are necessary but neither restored the menu by itself; the dominant cause was always menu-too-tall.
45	
46	## Root cause
47	
48	`display-menu` does not paginate. tmux measures the rendered popup height; if it exceeds available terminal height (after `status-position` and `-y` anchor offset), the popup is suppressed entirely with no log message. There is no scroll, no truncation, no error event.
49	
50	Why this is hard to diagnose:
51	- A static config + a tall terminal means it works "always" → no one notices the limit until they ssh in from a small pane / mobile shell / split layout.
52	- Adding rows over time keeps it working until one row tips it over → looks like "the new row broke something".
53	- Bisecting a long menu by halving the rows works (because the half is short enough to render) → looks like a content problem.
54	
55	## Workaround
56	
57	Two changes:
58	
59	1. **Generate the menu from a script** that reads `#{client_height}` and emits a tier-trimmed row list:
60	   - Tier 0 (always): ~7 highest-frequency rows
61	   - Tier 1 (height ≥ 22): adds new-window/split/zoom
62	   - Tier 2 (height ≥ 14): adds submenu launchers + cheatsheet/key-search
63	2. **Push everything else into submenus**, each implemented as its own `tmux display-menu` script. Submenus get a fresh quoting context, so nested escaping disasters go away.
64	
65	Layout in this repo:
66	
67	```
68	~/.config/tmux/menu.sh           # top menu (tier-aware)
69	~/.config/tmux/menu-layouts.sh   # → Layouts submenu
70	~/.config/tmux/menu-session.sh   # → Session mgmt submenu
71	~/.config/tmux/menu-sesh.sh      # → Sesh extras submenu
72	~/.config/tmux/menu-popups.sh    # → Popups submenu
73	~/.config/tmux/menu-theme.sh     # → Theme submenu
74	~/.config/tmux/menu-system.sh    # → System submenu (reload, plugins, detach, clock)
75	~/.config/tmux/sesh-picker.sh    # nested fzf-tmux extracted out
76	~/.config/tmux/sesh-windows.sh   # nested fzf-tmux extracted out
77	```
78	
79	Bindings in `dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf`:
80	
81	```tmux
82	bind-key Space run-shell "~/.config/tmux/menu.sh"
83	bind-key e     run-shell "~/.config/tmux/menu.sh"
84	```
85	
86	When adding a new menu item, add it to the relevant submenu, not the top menu. Top-menu cap is ~14 rows (fits a 20-row terminal). When adding a row that contains `{`, `}`, `;`, backticks, or more than two levels of nested quotes, extract to a script.
87	
88	## Prevention
89	
90	When designing a tmux popup menu:
91	
92	1. **Cap the top menu at ~14 rows.** Use submenus (separate `display-menu` scripts) for everything else.
93	2. **Generate the menu from a script** that consults `#{client_height}` and `#{client_width}` if you want auto-trim across many heights.
94	3. **Verify by shrinking the terminal vertically.** A "menu works" smoke test on a full-height window does not catch this.
95	4. **Don't blame key encoding first.** If a `display-menu` binding doesn't fire, bind the same `display-menu` to a known-good letter key on a known-tall terminal — if it works there, the problem is height (or content), not the key.
96	5. **For complex commands inside menu rows** (any `{`, `}`, `;`, backtick, nested fzf binds): extract to a script.
97	
98	## Related
99	
100	- `dot_config/tmux/executable_menu.sh` — top-level menu generator (height-aware)
101	- `dot_config/tmux/executable_menu-*.sh` — submenu scripts
102	- `dot_config/tmux/executable_sesh-picker.sh`, `executable_sesh-windows.sh` — extracted complex commands
103	- `dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf` — `bind-key Space` / `bind-key e` → `menu.sh`
104	- [`AGENTS.md` → Tmux ≥ 3.3 required for popup menu](../AGENTS.md) — adjacent invariant about a different `display-menu` failure mode (off-screen on tmux 3.2a). The 3.3+ position-clamping fix doesn't help with menu-too-tall — that limit is independent.
105	- `man tmux` → `display-menu` → "If the menu is too large to fit on the terminal, it is not displayed."
106

```md
# tmux server exits when entering copy-mode (3.6a homebrew bottle, macOS)

**Symptoms** (grep this section):

- Status line shows `[server exited unexpectedly]` after a long-running session (anywhere from ~100 minutes to ~8 days uptime)
- Triggers when entering copy-mode (`prefix + [` by default; in this repo also via `prefix + b` / scroll wheel / clicking on past output to enter selection)
- All panes / windows / sessions die at once — `tmux ls` after the crash returns `no server running on /private/tmp/tmux-501/default`
- macOS Diagnostic Report at `~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/tmux-YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS.ips` contains:
  - `"signal":"SIGABRT"` / `"indicator":"Abort trap: 6"` / `"type":"EXC_CRASH"`
  - `___BUG_IN_CLIENT_OF_LIBMALLOC_POINTER_BEING_FREED_WAS_NOT_ALLOCATED` in the symbol list (libmalloc abort = double-free or invalid free)
  - Stack frames in this exact order: `cmd_copy_mode_exec` → `window_pane_set_mode` → `window_copy_init` → `window_copy_clone_screen` → `screen_reinit` → `grid_clear_lines` → `grid_free_line`
  - `"asi": {"libsystem_c.dylib": ["crashed on child side of fork pre-exec"]}` — appears in every report; **unrelated diagnostic noise from libsystem_c**, not the actual fault. Don't chase.
  - `slice_uuid: 1b2d8e7b-bb77-3465-8bab-73f5bbaffe49` — fingerprint of the homebrew `tmux 3.6a` bottle. If your `.ips` has this UUID, you have this exact bug.
- Terminal **does not matter** — upstream reports include alacritty, ghostty, iTerm2; locally we hit it under alacritty.
- `tmux-resurrect` saved snapshot is intact — relaunching `tmux` + `tmux-continuum` restores layout, but in-pane process state (agent conversations, nvim buffers) is lost.

**First seen**: 2026-04-28 (locally; upstream first report 2025-12-23)
**Affects**: `tmux 3.6a` homebrew stable bottle on macOS 26.x / Apple Silicon. Issue is **terminal-agnostic and CPU-vendor-agnostic** within Apple Silicon (M3 Max / M4 Pro / Mac16,10 all confirmed upstream).
**Status**: **fixed upstream** in commit [`035a2f3`](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/commit/035a2f35d40628dcfe235179220fc0ede848a195) (2026-01-06); **not yet released as a tagged version** — homebrew `tmux 3.6a` bottle is the latest stable as of 2026-04 and still ships the bug.

## Symptom

After a long-running tmux session (uptime varies wildly: 100 minutes locally, 12 hours, 25 hours, 8 days in upstream reports), entering copy-mode aborts the entire tmux server with `Abort trap: 6`. From the user's POV: **the terminal redraws once, the tmux status bar disappears, and you're back in the bare login shell**. All sessions, all panes, all running processes die simultaneously.

The `.ips` Diagnostic Report shows libmalloc abort during `grid_free_line` — i.e. tmux is freeing a grid line whose backing allocation was already freed (or was never on the heap). The release path is initiated by copy-mode entry: when you press `prefix + [`, tmux clones the current screen into a copy-mode-owned screen via `window_copy_clone_screen`, which calls `screen_reinit` → `grid_clear_lines` → `grid_free_line` on the destination grid before populating it with the cloned content. The double-free triggers there.

## Root cause

A bug in `screen_reinit` / `grid_clear_lines` introduced in the 3.6 line. Long-running sessions accumulate the precondition (specifics in the upstream commit) and entering copy-mode triggers the abort. Fixed in [tmux/tmux@035a2f3](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/commit/035a2f35d40628dcfe235179220fc0ede848a195).

Upstream tracking: [tmux/tmux#4777](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/issues/4777) — closed 2026-01-06, fix verified by reporters running master for ~2 weeks without recurrence ([comment](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/issues/4777#issuecomment-3784173705)).

## Workaround

**Until tmux 3.7 / 3.6b ships** with the fix, switch the local install to `--HEAD`:

\```bash
# 1. Save anything you care about — running tmux server must die.
tmux ls                          # confirm what's running first

# 2. Kill the server (otherwise the new binary won't be picked up;
#    a running tmux server keeps the old binary mapped in memory).
tmux kill-server

# 3. Reinstall from master.
brew install --HEAD tmux
# OR if already installed: brew reinstall --HEAD tmux

# 4. Verify.
tmux -V                          # should show "tmux next-3.7" or similar (HEAD marker)
which tmux                       # /opt/homebrew/bin/tmux
\```

After 3.7 (or 3.6b) is tagged on homebrew-core, revert to the bottle:

\```bash
tmux kill-server
brew uninstall tmux
brew install tmux                # back to stable bottle (no --HEAD)
tmux -V                          # confirm 3.7+ or 3.6b
\```

### Trade-offs of `--HEAD`

- **No bottle, no `brew upgrade` auto-pull.** `brew upgrade tmux` won't refresh a `--HEAD` install with new master commits. To pick up new fixes you must `brew reinstall --HEAD tmux` (which downloads the latest master and rebuilds locally).
- **Local build means Xcode CLT is required.** `xcode-select --install` if you don't already have it; the user already does on this Mac.
- **ABI churn risk.** When dependencies (libevent, ncurses, openssl, utf8proc) get bumped by `brew upgrade`, a `--HEAD`-built binary may need `brew reinstall --HEAD tmux` to relink. If `tmux` starts segfaulting at startup after an unrelated `brew upgrade`, the relink fixed it 99% of the time.
- **Master can break.** Upstream tmux master is generally stable but is not a release. If you hit a different bug, `brew uninstall tmux && brew install tmux` returns to 3.6a (which has *this* bug — pick your poison until 3.7 ships).

## Why ansible / Linuxbrew / tmux-appimage paths are not affected

The repo's Linux upgrade paths in [`dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml`](../dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml#L1933-L1953) (Linuxbrew or `nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage`) target a **different** tmux problem (the 3.2a popup-clamp invariant in `AGENTS.md` → "Tmux ≥ 3.3 required for popup menu"). They install whatever Linuxbrew ships (also 3.6a today, also vulnerable on Apple-Silicon-Linux ARM hosts in theory) or whatever `tmux-appimage` cuts (currently 3.4 — older, may also be vulnerable but no upstream reports on Linux yet).

If a Linux host hits the same `.ips`-equivalent (Linux core dump showing the same stack), the workaround on Linuxbrew hosts is the same: `brew install --HEAD tmux`. On `tmux-appimage` hosts, build from source manually until 3.7 lands. Don't preemptively retrofit; only one upstream user has ever reported hitting this on Linux.

## Prevention

- **Don't paper over with config.** No `set -g …` change in `dot_config/tmux/common.conf` mitigates this — it's a heap bug in the binary, not a config-driven behaviour.
- **Don't avoid copy-mode.** Restricting your own muscle memory is not a real workaround for a daily driver tool.
- **Watch for the tmux 3.7 (or 3.6b) tag.** When it lands on `homebrew-core`, switch back to bottle (steps above). [TODO entry](../TODO.md) tracks this.
- **If a new machine joins the fleet with macOS + Apple Silicon + tmux installed via `brew install tmux`**, follow the workaround proactively (one `brew reinstall --HEAD tmux` saves a 100-minute-to-8-day surprise later).

## Related

- Upstream issue: [tmux/tmux#4777](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/issues/4777)
- Upstream fix commit: [`035a2f3`](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/commit/035a2f35d40628dcfe235179220fc0ede848a195)
- [`AGENTS.md` → Tmux ≥ 3.3 required for popup menu](../AGENTS.md) — adjacent invariant about a **different** tmux version-related failure (popup-clamp on 3.2a). The 3.3 floor doesn't help here; this bug requires 3.7 (or `--HEAD`).
- [`pitfalls/tmux-resurrect-agents.md`](tmux-resurrect-agents.md) — what's lost when the server dies (layout restored, agent conversation state isn't).
- [`pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md`](tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md) — another "tmux silently fails with no error" trap (different cause, similar mental model: don't blame your config first).
- [`pitfalls/yazi-tmux-popup-crash.md`](yazi-tmux-popup-crash.md) — the *other* known way to crash the tmux server in this repo's setup (display-popup + yazi). Different stack, different fix; cross-linked because both produce `[server exited unexpectedly]`.
- macOS triage: `~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/tmux-*.ips` (JSONL — `head -1` is the manifest, body is a single JSON blob with `threads[0].frames`). Compare `slice_uuid` to identify the binary; compare `frames` to identify the stack.
